chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from al-Wasshaq from Ahmad ibn A'idh from Abu al-Hasan al-Sawwaq from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
O Aban! When you arrive in Kufa, narrate this hadith: 'Whoever testifies that there is no god except Allah, sincerely, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.'
I said to him, 'People of every type come to me. Should I narrate this hadith to all of them?'

He said, 'Yes, O Aban! On the Day of Judgment, when Allah gathers the first and the last, the phrase 'La ilaha illa Allah' will be stripped from them, except for the one who was upon this matter (Wilayah/Imamate).'

key_terms.الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ: The first and the last (of creation)
key_terms.مُخْلِصاً: Sincerely/Making the testimony pure from shirk

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Paradise regarding the testimony of 'La ilaha illa Allah' according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Aban ibn Taghlib from Imam al-Sadiq (as), establishes that mere verbal declaration of Tawhid is insufficient for salvation without the accompanying reality of Wilayah. The Imam illustrates this by describing how 'La ilaha illa Allah' will be stripped from the lips of the majority on the Day of Judgment, retaining only for those who remained steadfast upon the specific matter of divine authority. This underscores the Shia theological principle that true monotheism is inextricably linked to recognizing and adhering to the Imams as the rightful successors of the Prophet.
